concept: One turn of a conversation: the reader's on chosen glass at the end edge, the answer as text on the pane, its steps above and quiet actions under it.

default_to_avoid.pattern: a chat message as a pair of coloured bubbles, blue for the reader and grey for the bot
default_to_avoid.kind: chat message, chat bubble, conversation turn, message row
default_to_avoid.why_not: two coloured bubbles put a hue on both sides and box the answer in; Pane keeps the answer as content on the pane and marks only the reader's turn with chosen glass

derivation.consequence: the scene supplies the hue; the system owns no hue of its own, only white at opacities and one ink, and colour appears only where it states a status or marks a diagram
derivation.form: the answer is content, so it sits as text on the pane with no bubble of its own

derivation.consequence: light falls from above, so every surface carries a rim brightest along its top edge and a soft shadow below that says where it floats, and a recess is the inverse, shaded under its top lip and lit on its bottom lip; a nested surface adds no second blur, because one sheet of glass is one layer
derivation.form: the reader's turn is chosen glass, the system's mark for what the reader chose

derivation.consequence: labels and names exist for assistive tech even when hidden visually
derivation.form: the author is read first and a streaming answer is marked busy until it is complete

variants.reason: A keeps the answer as content and marks the reader's turn without a hue (P1, P3). B adds two hues. C loses who said what at a glance.

root.why: a turn is a row; the reader's sits at the end edge and the answer at the start

user.why: the reader's turn moves to the end edge

assistant.why: the answer takes the full width of the pane, because it is the content

avatar.why: an assistant may sign its turn with a small avatar before it

body.why: the head, steps, text and actions stack at the small gap

head.why: who and when sit above the text at caption size in the secondary tone

author.why: the author is medium weight so the turn can be found by who said it

time.why: the time uses tabular figures so times line up

text.why: the text wraps anywhere so a long link or code never spills out

caret.why: a caret follows a streaming answer and blinks slowly, so the reader sees it is still arriving

actions.why: copy and retry are quiet ghost buttons under the answer, never louder than it

steps.why: the steps the assistant took sit above its answer as rows that open

tool.why: a step is a quiet tinted row with the inner corner

toolHead.why: the step's line is a 44px summary that opens its detail

toolTitle.why: the step reads as a past-tense line in the reader's words, never as code

toolBody.why: the detail is label size in the secondary tone

mark.why: each step state has its own glyph shape: a turning arc, a check, an octagon

running.why: a running step turns slowly so the reader sees the assistant is still at it

done.why: a finished step takes the positive mark beside its check, so done reads by shape too

failed.why: a failed step takes the critical mark beside its octagon, so a failure reads by shape too

sr.why: the state word is read before the line, so the state is never colour or shape alone

focus-visible.why: the focus ring shows on a step's line when it is reached by keyboard

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: under reduced motion nothing turns, blinks or breathes, and the word carries the news

@media forced-colors: active.why: in forced colours the system draws the edges and marks, so every part stays findable

@blink.why: the caret blinks in steps so it reads as a cursor and never pulses

@turn.why: a running step turns once a second or so, steady and never frantic
